Core prices (excluding food, energy and trade) rose 0.5%, same as September.

points: Warsh set out three AI scenarios, including one where AI disappoints, shares fall and unemployment rises; he stressed they are not forecasts.
He did not discuss interest rates or the hot October inflation report (AP).
Scotiabank's Derek Holt said Governor Waller is alone in backing a half-point December hike (KuCoin News).
Gold eased about 0.9% on the day.

affects.why: Nvidia is the All-World fund's largest holding at 5.0% (Vanguard).
First report without Huang; Nvidia says roadmap and customer commitments continue without interruption (Nvidia 8-K).

calendar.beat_record: Beat EPS in 7 of the last 8 quarters (MarketBeat).
downside: CNBC (16 Nov): board not considering Huang's return; outside law firm reviewing his conduct (The Next Web).
Huang resigned on 12 Nov; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and a permanent search is under way (Nvidia 8-K). Shares closed at $166.19 after a $148.80 low (CoinDesk).
WSJ reported on 11 Nov the board is preparing to oust Huang; shares fell about 8% after hours to around $160 (Yahoo Finance, StockTitan).
Three customers are 44% of revenue; purchase commitments up to $279bn; gross margin guided lower; no China data-centre sales assumed (XTB).
The board opened an independent probe on 8 Nov into reports Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence; House chairs want a briefing on 18 Nov (NBC, FourWeekMBA).
Trump said on 9 Nov the FBI is looking into Huang's relationship with the alleged spy, though he said he believes Huang (Al Jazeera).
calendar.expected: EPS $2.49, revenue $108.8bn (MarketBeat), just above Nvidia's own $108bn ±2% guide; gross margin guided 74%.

history_sources.name: Regards of Wall Street NVDA earnings moves

key_metrics.why: Beating its own guide is expected
Historically the main driver of the move

means: Nvidia guided $108bn revenue and a 74% gross margin; the consensus ($108.8bn) is only just above its own guide.
It beat in 7 of the last 8 quarters but the shares fell after 5 of them. What moves it is the outlook for the next quarter, not the beat.
Last quarter it rose 8.7% after guiding well above forecasts. That is the pattern to look for.
Its results also move your grid ETF and your Vanguard fund, where Nvidia is one of the largest holdings.
past_notes: Q1 FY26: EPS shown as a miss only because of a $4.5bn China export charge; underlying EPS $0.96 beat.
Q2 FY27 (Aug): rose 8.7% after guiding well above forecasts.

result.headline: Beat on revenue, EPS and guidance, but shares closed 2.9% lower on 18 Nov after a 4.8% after-hours gain
points: Revenue $115.8bn vs ~$109bn expected (+103% a year); adjusted EPS $2.68 vs ~$2.48 (TipRanks).
Next-quarter guide $130bn ±3% vs ~$125bn expected, a quarter with an extra week (Nvidia release, Coinpaper).
Gross margin guided down to 71-72% from 74.9%, and still no China data-centre sales assumed (Nvidia release).
The 4.8% extended-trading gain reversed: shares closed down 2.89% at $150.96, which Yahoo Finance ties to leadership worries after Huang's exit.
For you: strong numbers did not lift the shares this time; sources say the CEO question is what investors are focused on. Nvidia is also VWRP's largest holding.

upside: Last quarter's guide was well above consensus, and the CFO pointed to ~70% growth in FY28 vs ~44% expected (XTB).
calendar.watch_line: Watch: next quarter's revenue guide and gross margin in the first report under interim CEO Colette Kress

result.headline: In line: +0.2% headline; control group +0.6% beat 0.4% forecast
points: Headline +0.2% as expected; September unrevised at +0.8% (Reuters).
Control group +0.6% vs 0.4% expected; September revised up to 0.5% (Reuters).
Import prices +1.1% vs 0.7% expected, adding to inflation worries (Reuters, MarketScreener).
US shares still fell, led by tech before Nvidia's results (Kiplinger).

result.headline: Unemployment fell to 4.6% from 4.7%; regular pay growth slowed to 3.5%
points: Unemployment 4.6% in July-September, down 0.3 points on the quarter (ONS).
Regular pay growth 3.5% (from 3.7%); total pay 3.6% (ONS).
Vacancies down 3% to about 690,000; October payrolls early estimate down 34,000 (ONS).
FTSE 100 still ended 1.8% lower on global tech weakness (MarketScreener).

result.headline: 3.6%, as the consensus listed here expected (some forecasts were 3.7%)
points: CPI 3.6% from 3.5%; motor fuels the biggest upward push (Mortgage Solutions).
Core steady at 2.8%; services 3.7% vs the BoE's 3.9% projection (Yahoo Finance UK).
Deutsche Bank: gives the BoE 'some breathing space'; still sees CPI above 4% early next year.
The pound slipped to about $1.314 and the FTSE 100 fell 1.3%, led by miners.

points: Almost all officials judged further rate rises likely appropriate (CNBC via StockTitan).
A couple said a hike bigger than 0.25 points could be considered in December if data are unfavourable.
Almost all discussed the risk that AI investment returns could disappoint.
Gold fell to a 14-month low on the day as hike bets built (Ecofin).

points: Priced at $83, above the $70-78 range, raising a record $81.3bn from about 980m shares.
Opened at $111.50, fell as low as about $93 by early afternoon, then closed up 17.1%; market value about $1.3tn, around 40x trailing sales.
Amazon (about 1.9bn ANT shares) fell 3.9% and Alphabet (about 1.8bn) fell 3.5% as the wider market reversed.
Analyst Luke Lango: the debut shows AI funding is still flowing, but does not by itself end the AI sell-off.

upside: Renaissance Capital: $100 by the first close would be a 'solid pop'; toward $140 would signal renewed AI enthusiasm (CBS News).

calendar.expected: Autodesk's own guide: revenue $2.125-2.140bn, non-GAAP EPS $3.04-3.09. Consensus EPS $3.07 on $2.13bn revenue; whisper $3.16 (Earnings Whispers, 16 Nov). First quarter including MaintainX.

key_metrics.why: It has beaten its guide every quarter here
Future contracted revenue: the market's worry
Cuts here would hit the shares

means: Autodesk beat forecasts in all 8 of the last quarters, but the shares rose after only 4.
In its last two reports it beat yet fell about 4% each time, because full-year guidance came in light and future contracted revenue (cRPO) slowed to 12% growth from 18-20%.
So the key numbers are cRPO and the free-cash-flow guide ($2.725-2.750bn for the year), not the EPS beat.
You hold it for a few months, so this report falls inside your holding window.
past_notes: Q1 and Q2 FY27: beat both times, but fell ~4% each time on light guidance and slowing cRPO.

Jensen Huang's exit is cited as one factor weighing on the AI sector (source 1).

sources.title: Asian shares head for worst week since 2020 as AI rout deepens

stories.summary: MSCI's Asia-Pacific index fell 2.5% on Friday and is down 7% this week, its worst week since March 2020. Japan's Nikkei dropped 4.1% and South Korea's KOSPI 4.7%, following Wall Street's 2% fall. S&P 500 futures were down 0.4% and Nasdaq futures 0.7%, and an analyst said Anthropic's IPO had not eased worries about the AI trade.

impacts.why: Nvidia is named as a company whose chips are affected by the rule (source 2); Huang is due before lawmakers on 26 Nov (source 1).

sources.title: China hoards Nvidia's AI chips as US curbs remote access
China says it will take countermeasures if US imposes new chip curbs

stories.summary: A new US rule requires a licence to ship advanced AI chips to data centres in countries such as Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia that serve Chinese-headquartered firms. Asia Times reports Nvidia has cut its approved Asian buyer list by more than half and requires partners to track chip locations. China's commerce ministry said it would retaliate if the US pressed on.

Reuters puts it down to a dollar near a 19-month high and bets on a December Fed hike. A Capital.com analyst said there seems to be forced selling across markets.

stories.headline: UK retail sales due at 7am, with economists expecting a flat October

sources.title: UK Retail Sales Preview: Consensus Sees Flat October

stories.summary: Economists expect October retail volumes unchanged on the month and up 1.7% on the year, after a 0.4% fall in September. The Bank of England raised rates to 4% this month; a weak figure would test the case for another rise, a strong one would support it.

topline: Asian shares are heading for their worst week since March 2020 (Nikkei -4.1%, KOSPI -4.7%) and US futures are lower again after Thursday's 2% Nasdaq fall; the Nasdaq is about 13.4% below its 6 Oct high, VWRP 6.2% below its high.
Gold fell another 1.9% overnight to about $3,552, down about 8.9% this week, which will weigh on SGLN when London opens.
A December Fed hike is now about 97% priced after Philadelphia Fed's Paulson said rates must rise again.
Grab's 6.7% fall on Thursday came with the market sell-off; no company news was found. ARK sold more Nvidia and bought Anthropic.
Coming up: UK retail sales at 7am today, Autodesk results after the US close on Tuesday 24 Nov (consensus EPS $3.07).
